title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck computes an 'orbifold' or 'mass' class of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Spec Z. The class lives in a Grothendieck group K_!(Z) of schemes over Z with rational coefficients. A stratum whose geometric points have automorphism group G contributes [stratum]/|G|.

Setup:
- The coarse space is the j-line E^1, with [E^1] = T(1), the Tate/Lefschetz class L.
- It is cut along two sections, both isomorphic to Spec Z: S_0 (j = 1728, Aut = Z/4) and S_1 (j = 0, Aut = Z/6).
- These sections meet in a_2 (characteristic 2, Aut of order 24, i.e. SL_2(F_3) semidirect Z/4... order 24) and a_3 (characteristic 3, Aut of order 12).
- The generic stratum U has Aut = Z/2.
- He sets ζ_p = [Spec F_p] = i_{p!}(1), the push-forward from K_!(F_p) to K_!(Z).

Computation:
- [U] = L - 2 + ζ_2 + ζ_3.
- [S_0'] = [S_1'] = 1 - ζ_2 - ζ_3.
- [M_{1,1}] = (1/2)[U] + (1/4 + 1/6)[S'] + (1/24)ζ_2 + (1/12)ζ_3 = (1/2)(L - 1) - 1/12 + (1/8)ζ_2 + (1/6)ζ_3.
- Adding the cusp, which has weight 1/2 (Aut = ±1), gives [\hat M_{1,1}] = L/2 - 1/12 + ζ_2/8 + ζ_3/6. This is formula (80).

What it serves: it is part of a systematic computation of such classes for the strata 'à l'infini' of \hat M_{g,ν}. The next page passes to \hat M_{0,5}.

Specialisations:
- Under L ↦ 1 and ζ_p ↦ 0 (complex Euler characteristic), one gets χ_orb(M_{1,1}) = -1/12 = ζ(-1) (Harer–Zagier). For the compactification one gets χ_orb(\bar M_{1,1}) = 5/12. So the page gives an arithmetic, motivic refinement of the orbifold Euler characteristic.
- The refinement carries explicit correction terms at the primes 2 and 3.
errors: The machine transcription's '7/6 [S'_1]' should be '1/6 [S'_1]'. The overbrace explicitly sums 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12. With 1/6 the arithmetic is correct: the ζ_2 coefficient is 1/2 - 5/12 + 1/24 = 1/8, and the ζ_3 coefficient is 1/2 - 5/12 + 1/12 = 1/6.

Possible inconsistency with (79) on the previous page. There the class over Z[1/2] is given as (1/2)(T(1) - 1) - 1/12, with no ζ_3 term. Over Z[1/2], ζ_2 vanishes but ζ_3 does not, so (80) predicts an extra (1/6)ζ_3. (79) is correct only over Z[1/6], or the earlier computation overlooked characteristic 3.

The calculation is formal: it assumes the class is additive over the stratification of the coarse space weighted by 1/|Aut|. This invariant differs from Ekedahl's class of the stack, for which [M_{1,1}] = L. It is a choice of invariant rather than an error.

ideas.what: Class of a Deligne–Mumford stack in a rational Grothendieck group of Z-schemes. Each stratum of the coarse space is weighted by 1/|geometric automorphism group|.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold/stacky motivic class (mass-weighted constructible class); motivic lift of the orbifold Euler characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ekedahl (Grothendieck group of stacks, 2009), Behrend (stacky point counts), and others in different forms

ideas.what: Stratification of the j-line over Spec Z by automorphism groups (Z/2, Z/4, Z/6, and orders 24 and 12 in characteristics 2 and 3).
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism groups of elliptic curves (Deuring; Silverman, Appendix A)

ideas.what: ζ_p = [Spec F_p] = i_{p!}(1) as fibre-correction classes in K_0(Var/Z). This gives the explicit formula [M_{1,1}] = (L - 1)/2 - 1/12 + ζ_2/8 + ζ_3/6 and [\hat M_{1,1}] = L/2 - 1/12 + ζ_2/8 + ζ_3/6.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic refinement of χ_orb(M_{1,1}) = -1/12 and χ_orb(\bar M_{1,1}) = 5/12
ideas.usually_credited_to: The Euler characteristic values are due to Harer–Zagier (1986) and classical sources; the explicit Z-refinement is unsure

missed.claim: An explicit 'motivic orbifold class' of M_{1,1} and \bar M_{1,1} over Spec Z. It includes correction terms at the bad primes 2 and 3 (ζ_2/8 + ζ_3/6), and it specialises to the Harer–Zagier values -1/12 and 5/12. Grothendieck thus had a framework of mass-weighted classes in K_!(Z) for the strata of \hat M_{g,ν}, apparently independently of and before the later stacky Grothendieck-ring literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Arithmetic (over Z rather than over a field) motivic Euler characteristics of moduli stacks, with explicit bad-fibre terms, are rarely written down. The ζ_p bookkeeping gives a concrete model for tracking small-characteristic phenomena in classes of M_{g,n}.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is elementary and checks out. However, a systematic programme of 1/|Aut|-weighted classes over Spec Z, refining orbifold Euler characteristics with prime-by-prime corrections, is a notable unpublished detail that I do not know to be credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: '[E']' should read '[E^1]' (the j-line, i.e. affine line).
'K_!(Z_p)' should read 'K_!(Z/pZ)', i.e. K_!(F_p); likewise ζ_p = [Spec Z/pZ].
The garbled line is probably 'où en général on pose, pour un nombre premier p'.
The struck symbol after -7/12 is a crossed-out numeral (probably 4). The struck coefficient of ζ_2 is replaced by 1/8.
